top.tourTip: A quick tour of how MyRGB works
settings.vendorApps.title: Vendor apps
settings.vendorApps.brandAppsLikeIcue: Brand apps like iCUE, G HUB and Armoury Crate also try to control your lights, and they fight with MyRGB. Once MyRGB runs a brand's devices you can usually uninstall its app. Here's what's on this PC, and what each app does that MyRGB doesn't.
settings.vendorApps.uninstallConfirm: This opens {0}’s own uninstaller. Windows will probably ask for permission. Your MyRGB presets and settings are not affected.
settings.appearance.title: Appearance
settings.appearance.pickALookFor: Pick a look for MyRGB. It changes right away; your lights don't change.
settings.language.title: Language
settings.language.about: The language MyRGB's screens use. Translations are written by people who use MyRGB; anything not translated yet shows in English.
settings.language.restartNote: MyRGB will show {0} the next time it starts.
settings.account.title: Account
settings.account.anAccountIsOptional: An account is optional. Sign in to keep your presets in sync across PCs, share presets with the community, and contact Root Labs. MyRGB never sees your password: you sign in on the provider's own page in your browser.
settings.account.thisPermanentlyDeletesY: This permanently deletes your account, your synced presets and any presets you shared. Presets on this PC stay. It can't be undone.
settings.supportMyrgb.title: Support MyRGB
settings.supportMyrgb.myrgbIsFreeAnd: MyRGB is free and open source, and every feature in it, fan control included, stays free. If it replaced a few vendor apps for you, chipping in keeps it going: it pays for the servers behind sync and the community, and for time to support more hardware.
settings.supportMyrgb.supportersGetABadg: Supporters get a badge on the presets they share, and room to sync up to 200 presets and share up to 15 (everyone gets 50 and 5).
settings.supportMyrgb.showMySupporterBad: Show my supporter badge on shared presets
settings.supportMyrgb.supportWithTheSame: Support with the same email as your MyRGB account, so your perks can be matched to it.
settings.startup.title: Startup
settings.startup.closingTheWindowNever: Closing the window never quits MyRGB; it keeps your lights running from the tray. Quit from the tray icon's menu.
settings.updates.title: Updates
settings.updates.checkForUpdatesWhen: Check for updates when MyRGB starts
settings.updates.updatesDownloadFromThe: Updates download from the project's GitHub releases and install in place; Windows never asks for permission. A download is checked against the checksum published with the release before it runs.
settings.idleDimming.title: Idle dimming
settings.idleDimming.lightsFadeDownAfter: Lights fade down after you step away from the keyboard and mouse, and come straight back the moment you touch either.
settings.lightsOut.title: Lights out
settings.lightsOut.offWhileWindowsIs: Off while Windows is locked or asleep
settings.lightsOut.yourLightsGoDark: Your lights go dark and come back on their own. Turning them on in the meantime (here, from the tray, a hotkey or a Stream Deck) keeps them on until the next lock, sleep or night.
settings.monitors.title: Monitors
settings.monitors.presetsSetTheirOwn: Presets set their own monitor brightness
settings.monitors.twoMonitorsAtThe: Two monitors at the same number rarely look alike. Give each its own darkest and brightest, and the slider runs between them, so 0% is each one's darkest and 100% its brightest.
settings.monitors.nightUsesTheTimes: Night uses the times under Lights out. Night wins over the lights, which win over a preset's level, which wins over the slider. A change you make with the monitor's own buttons stays until one of these has a reason to change it. The local API has the same control: GET or POST /api/monitors.
settings.appProfiles.title: App profiles
settings.appProfiles.whenOneOfThese: When one of these programs is in the foreground, MyRGB switches to its preset, and switches back when you leave it.
settings.schedule.title: Schedule
settings.schedule.atEachTimeMyrgb: At each time, MyRGB switches to that preset and keeps it until the next one; pick something else in between and it stays until then. When MyRGB starts, it picks up wherever the day has got to. App profiles still win while their program is in front.
settings.globalHotkeys.title: Global hotkeys
settings.globalHotkeys.useKeyboardShortc: Use keyboard shortcuts from any app
settings.smoothness.title: Smoothness
settings.smoothness.30LooksSmoothFor: 30 looks smooth for every effect. Higher uses more USB bandwidth, and some wireless devices can't keep up.
settings.videoWallpapers.title: Video wallpapers
settings.videoWallpapers.yourGraphicsCar: Your graphics card has a small part built just for playing video. With this on, it does the hard work of a video wallpaper, the same way it does when you watch a video in your browser, and your processor stays free for everything else (it usually takes most of the work off it). Leave it on unless a video wallpaper flickers, shows the wrong colors or won't play; then turn it off and your processor plays it instead. If the graphics card can't handle a video, MyRGB switches to the processor by itself.
settings.streamDeck.title: Stream Deck
settings.streamDeck.keysCanSwitchPresets: Keys can switch presets (showing each preset's colors), turn the lights on and off, and change brightness.
settings.help.title: Help
settings.help.questionsBugsOrA: Questions, bugs, or a device you'd like supported? Reach Root Labs through our website.
settings.advanced.title: Advanced
settings.advanced.myrgbStartsOpenrgbOut: MyRGB starts OpenRGB out of sight to reach most devices. Change this only if you use your own copy. Takes effect the next time MyRGB starts.
settings.advanced.localApiForScripts: Local API (for scripts and the Stream Deck plugin)
